chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who prays the voluntary prayers in the cities (or large towns) while he is on his mount, wherever it turns him towards, he said: 'Yes, there is no harm in it.'

key_terms.الْأَمْصَارِ: Cities or large towns (as opposed to open fields)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray voluntary prayers while riding a mount in a city, and does the direction of the animal determine the qibla?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the flexibility of voluntary prayer for travelers, permitting them to remain mounted and pray in the direction their beast naturally faces. This ruling alleviates the burden of travel by removing the strict requirement to dismount or manually align with the qibla for nafl prayers, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease (taysir) in transit.
